question: I run a delivery business and want to plan routes for my fleet. Help me set this up as an optimization problem.
ground_truth: The problem is severely underspecified. Before formulating anything, the agent MUST surface all required information across the five data categories — it must NOT silently default to VRP, invent capacities or time windows, or jump to code. Specifically, the agent must ask the user about: (1) PROBLEM TYPE — single vehicle visiting all stops (TSP), multiple vehicles with capacity/time constraints (VRP), or pickup-then-deliver pairs (PDP)? (2) LOCATIONS data — how many locations, where is the depot (or are there multiple depots), and is there a cost/distance/travel-time matrix or coordinates to build one from? (3) ORDERS / TASKS — which locations must be visited, demand or service-time per stop? (4) FLEET — how many vehicles, capacity per vehicle (per dimension if multiple), start and end locations? (5) CONSTRAINTS — time windows for vehicles and orders, service times, precedence requirements? The agent does NOT produce code and does NOT pick one interpretation silently.
expected_behavior: Surfaces that the problem is underspecified — does NOT silently default to VRP, does NOT invent specific numbers (vehicle count, capacities, time windows, depot)
Asks about all five data categories before formulating: problem type (TSP/VRP/PDP), locations & cost/distance matrix, orders & demand, fleet & capacities, and constraints (time windows, precedence)
Does not produce code or an API call sequence — this is a conceptual / data-gathering response
